facts: Enter BMC U-Boot and run `dramtest 0` for over 12 hours.
Criterion only says BMC works normally afterward.
Machine time 7200 minutes conflicts with >12 hours.
source_snapshot.v2: MANUAL ONLY with vendor syntax and BMC recovery.

original_test_intent.statement: Stress BMC DRAM from U-Boot for more than 12 hours at 40 C/+5% rail margin and prove the BMC returns to normal service.
must_preserve: BMC, U-Boot `dramtest 0`, >12 hours and physical margin.
unknowns: Vendor command semantics/destructiveness, loop behavior, expected error count, 7200-minute metadata and recovery path.

v2_review_conclusion.specific_gap: It does not call out the extreme machine-time conflict or turn 'works normally' into concrete post-U-Boot service checks.

v3_review_conclusion.summary: Keep manual control; require vendor proof that `dramtest 0` is safe for this BMC and resolve the intended duration before entering U-Boot.

revision_candidate.test_name: Stress BMC DRAM in U-Boot at 40 C and +5% Rail Margin
revision_candidate.purpose: Run the vendor-defined BMC DRAM test for the approved duration and verify zero disallowed memory errors plus complete restoration of BMC management services.
revision_candidate.applicable_platform_environment: Exact BMC/U-Boot build with serial console and recovery, calibrated chamber and rail-margin fixtures.
revision_candidate.target_scope: BMC DRAM only; not host DDR. One supervised command instance for the owner-resolved duration.
revision_candidate.required_inputs: Vendor `dramtest 0` semantics, duration/loop/stop behavior, acceptable output, 12-hour versus 7200-minute decision, console/recovery credentials and fixture approval.
revision_candidate.test_command_procedure_intent: Preserve baseline, enter U-Boot through approved console, run exactly the signed DRAM test while operator records environment/output, exit through supported path and validate BMC services.
revision_candidate.preconditions: Host state is safe, alternate console/power recovery works, fixture limits and watchdog behavior are known.
revision_candidate.expected_evidence: Firmware/U-Boot identity, exact transcript/status/timestamps, continuous chamber/rail data, memory error summary, recovery actions, BMC boot completion, IPMI/Redfish/sensor/SEL/watchdog/network reachability and host management health.
revision_candidate.acceptance_reference: Signed vendor zero-error criteria and all named BMC services operational after return; mere console prompt is insufficient.
revision_candidate.safety_restrictions: Do not guess command behavior, clear SEL, enter U-Boot remotely without recovery or shorten/extend the owner duration.
revision_candidate.human_approval_requirements: BMC owner and lab operator approve command, outage, fixture and recovery.
revision_candidate.manual_boundaries: Console/fixture/recovery are operator actions; evidence parsing may be automated.
revision_candidate.recovery_requirements: Stop only by vendor method, restore nominal rails/temperature, recover BMC firmware/service via approved path and preserve transcript.
revision_candidate.stop_conditions: Unknown command semantics, fixture drift, memory error, console loss, BMC hang, unsafe temperature/power or failed service restoration.

identified_defects: Machine-time metadata is 120 hours, not >12 hours.
reason_for_change: The revision converts a vague recovery claim into enumerated BMC service evidence and prevents accidental 120-hour interpretation of a >12-hour U-Boot memory stress.
removed_ambiguities: Host DDR is excluded; BMC management services define recovery.
remaining_blockers: Vendor command and exact duration require owner decision.
objective_improvement_over_v2: V3 retains operator-only handling while making the duration discrepancy, BMC-versus-host memory boundary and post-stress service proof explicit.

per_case_integrity_check.source_specific_purpose_fact: Row 10 places `dramtest 0` in BMC U-Boot for >12 hours while metadata states 7200 minutes.
